units.title: 1 Introduction to the main travel and tourism definitions and concepts

outcomes.text: Define domestic, inbound and outbound tourism.
Define international tourism, day trips and short breaks and tell them apart.
Describe leisure travel and business travel (MICE).
Describe visiting friends and relatives (VFR) as a reason to travel.
Give examples of special interest travel such as medical, religious, adventure, cultural, sports and wellbeing.
Define sustainability and sustainable travel and tourism.
Define ecotourism and responsible tourism and compare them.
Distinguish products from services and explain why tourism is intangible and perishable.
Explain why tourism is seasonal and dynamic.
Explain why the industry is becoming more sustainable and resilient.
Describe business, leisure and special interest tourists.
Describe couples, families, groups, individuals and independent travellers.
Describe ecotourists, responsible tourists and tourists with specific needs.
Describe beach/coastal and island destinations.
Describe resorts: purpose-built, integrated, ski and eco.
Describe rural destinations (countryside, mountains, lakes) and urban ones (towns, cities).

topics.title: 2.1 The scale of travel and tourism

outcomes.text: Explain how economic factors such as disposable income and government investment affect tourism demand.
Explain how social factors such as demographics, health awareness and trends affect demand.
Explain how technology such as transport developments, IT and social media affects demand.
Explain how political factors such as terrorism, war, security and travel limits affect demand.
Explain how environmental factors such as sustainability concerns, extreme weather and disasters affect demand.
Explain how health risks such as disease and pandemics affect demand, and how these factors are managed.
Explain how changing customer attitudes and media influence grow sustainable tourism.
Explain how availability and promotion of sustainable products and government policies grow it.

topics.title: 2.2 Features of destinations and their appeal

outcomes.text: Explain how location, weather, seasons and topography attract different tourists.
Explain how accessibility and travel gateways and hubs affect appeal.
Explain how infrastructure such as public transport, roads, airports and ports affects appeal.
Describe built and natural attractions and their appeal.
Describe how culture (traditions, language, arts, music) and expected behaviours affect appeal.
Describe how tourism organisations, providers and sustainable provisions add to appeal.

topics.title: 2.3 Role of organisations in destination development and management

outcomes.text: Describe the role of government, ministries and local authorities.
Describe national tourism organisations (NTOs) and destination management companies (DMCs).
Describe non-government organisations (NGOs) and tourist information centres (TICs).
Explain how they encourage sustainable tourism, ensure resilience and manage risk.
Explain how they manage demand, make policy and plan.
Describe their marketing, branding and promotion of the destination.
Describe how they develop products, research, fund and provide information and advice.
Explain how they set standards and quality.

topics.title: 2.4 Factors affecting tourism development and management

outcomes.text: Explain the opportunities and constraints of the natural and built environment.
Explain sustainability (reduce, reuse, recycle) in development.
Explain risks and resilience.
Explain carrying capacity, overtourism and seasonality.
Describe economic objectives such as wealth, jobs and industry resilience.
Describe political objectives such as reputation and image.
Describe environmental objectives such as conservation and rejuvenation.
Describe sociocultural objectives such as protecting culture and good tourist-host relations.
Explain how to protect the natural and built environment: biodiversity, conservation, regeneration, visitor management, resource use, pollution limits.
Explain how to combat climate change: education programmes, recycling and reuse, reduced waste.
Explain how to empower communities: protecting culture, involving locals in decisions, training staff.
Explain how social enterprise supports local economies, community tourism and local jobs.

topics.title: 2.6 Economic, environmental and sociocultural impacts of travel and tourism

outcomes.text: Explain positive economic impacts: GDP, tax, wealth, living standards, multiplier effect, employment, infrastructure.
Explain negative economic impacts: inflation, leakage, seasonal jobs, opportunity cost, over-dependence.
Explain positive environmental impacts: investment, conservation, regeneration, awareness, visitor management, protection.
Explain negative environmental impacts: pollution, damage to flora and fauna, wildlife disturbance, habitat loss, resource depletion, litter, congestion.
Explain positive sociocultural impacts: preserved arts and crafts, community facilities, education, cultural understanding and pride.
Explain negative sociocultural impacts: changed way of life, lost identity, demonstration effect, commodification, crime, culture clash.

topics.title: 3.1 Role of tourism organisations, their sustainable practices, products, services and appeal

outcomes.text: Describe types of travel agent, independent tours and packages, and ancillary services.
Describe types of package holiday and what each package contains.
Describe types of accommodation provider, from hotels to camping and eco-friendly options.
Describe serviced (board basis) and self-catering accommodation, and occupancy rates.
Describe food and drink providers such as restaurants, cafes and street food.
Describe natural and built visitor attractions and events.
Describe ancillary providers: guided tours, currency exchange, car and bicycle hire.
Explain interrelationships between travel and tourism organisations.
Explain interdependencies between them.

topics.title: 3.3 Different types of transport and their appeal

outcomes.text: Describe air transport: charter, scheduled, low-cost, long and short haul.
Describe water transport such as ferries, cruises and water taxis.
Describe rail transport including trams, luxury trains and underground.
Describe road transport: car hire, taxis, coaches, buses and shuttles.

topics.title: 3.4 Sustainable developments within travel and transport

outcomes.text: Explain reduced emissions and carbon replacement schemes.
Describe alternative energy sources such as electricity and solar power.
Explain sustainable travel choices, such as transport method or domestic over international.

topics.title: 3.5 Domestic and international travel and transport infrastructure

outcomes.text: Explain the interdependency of transport methods.
Describe local public transport provision.
Describe ways of improving accessibility: express links, integrated transit, contactless payment, apps, hub airports.
Describe infrastructure that increases sustainability, such as cycle and bus lanes.
Describe alternative options such as bicycle and electric scooter rental.
Describe service delivery in different travel and tourism organisations.
Explain delivering service to different customer types.
Describe customer service standards and sustainability standards.
Explain the impact of good and bad customer service.
Describe procedures for handling complaints.
Describe handling enquiries such as directions, itineraries and recommendations.
Describe making reservations and taking payments.
Explain customer care policies and good product knowledge.

topics.title: 4.3 Provision of customer service for different types of tourists

outcomes.text: Explain access and information provision for tourists.
Describe provision for specific needs: mobility, visual, hearing, dietary, language and cultural.
Describe sustainably managed facilities and ancillary services.

topics.title: 4.4 Skills required when working in the travel and tourism industry

outcomes.text: Explain the types and importance of training, including sustainable practices.
Explain body language, personal presentation and languages.
Explain addressing the needs of responsible tourists.
Describe personal skills such as clear speech, numeracy, literacy, ICT and problem-solving.
Describe interpersonal skills such as listening, patience, teamwork and flexibility.

topics.title: 5.1 Importance of marketing to travel and tourism organisations

outcomes.text: Explain how marketing increases sales, profit, market share and customer base.
Explain competitive advantage and a positive sustainable image.
Explain customer satisfaction, brand loyalty and repeat business.
Explain target market and appropriate timing.
Explain cost, brand image and reputation such as industry awards.
Describe monitoring methods.
Describe products and services, including sustainable ones, and the product life cycle.
Describe promotion: campaigns, web and social media, brand, direct marketing, TV, radio and press.
Describe sales promotions, public relations, e-brochures and trade promotions.
Describe pricing strategies: penetration, skimming, discount, variable, loss leader, promotional, premium and bundling.
Describe distribution channels: direct, wholesalers, retailers, online.
Explain how physical location factors such as cost, features, staff and transport links matter.
Describe primary and secondary market research and qualitative and quantitative methods.
Use SWOT and PESTLE analysis.
Explain reasons for research: market position, customer needs, competitors, marketing plans.
Describe geographic market segments.
Describe demographic segments such as age, gender and income.
Describe psychographic (lifestyle) segments.
Develop a product and service mix for different segments.
Relate segments to customer type, quality and value for money.
Consider accessibility and sustainability when targeting.
